title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: PEcAn.benchmark toolkit provides modular framework aligning, evaluating, visualizing ecosystem model predictions observational benchmark datasets. tutorial walks complete workflow validation framework: 1. Understanding data intake schemas ensemble representation. 2. Generating simulated observations statistical error model known parameters. 3. Reshaping EFI long model predictions temporally aligning model observation data. 4. Computing statistical metrics ensemble mean (point metrics) full ensemble spread (probabilistic metrics). 5. Generating diagnostic plots (ribbon/spaghetti, scatter, residual plots) rendering automated Quarto validation scorecard. 6. Substituting custom model predictions observational data.

previous_headings: 1. Input Data Schemas and Ensemble Representation
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: Model ensemble outputs follow EFI (Ecological Forecasting Initiative) standard long format: datetime: Timestamp string (e.g. "2020-01-01 00:00:00"). site_id: Site identifier (e.g. "socs_sys1" "US-Ha1"). parameter: Integer index member ID ensemble member (e.g. 1, 2, ..., N). variable: CF/PEcAn standard variable name (e.g. "TotSoilCarb", "NEE", "GPP"). prediction: Model output numeric prediction value.

previous_headings: 1. Input Data Schemas and Ensemble Representation
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: Observational data require minimum: * date / time: Timestamp (POSIXct parseable string). * obs_mean / obvs: Observational numeric mean value. * obs_sd / obvs_sd (optional): Observational standard deviation / measurement error. * site_id / site (optional): Site identifier matching model dataset.

what: 2. Statistical Error Model and Fixture Generation
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: evaluate model metrics known true error parameterizations, simulated observations can generated using explicit statistical error model: ov,t=mv,t+Sv(βv+ϵv,t),ϵv,t∼N(0,τv2)o_{v,t} = m_{v,t} + S_v(\beta_v + \epsilon_{v,t}), \qquad \epsilon_{v,t} \sim N(0, \tau_v^2) : * ov,to_{v,t} simulated observation variable vv time tt; * mv,tm_{v,t} ensemble mean prediction; * SvS_v scale factor (standard deviation ensemble mean); * βv\beta_v relative bias parameter (e.g. 0.300.30, representing relative bias 30%30\%); * τv\tau_v relative random error standard deviation (e.g. 0.500.50, representing random noise equal 50%50\% variability).

previous_headings: 2. Statistical Error Model and Fixture Generation
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: PEcAn.benchmark, precomputed text fixtures provided package extdata: 1. simulated_observations.csv simulated_model_ensemble.csv: Synthetic dataset generated statistical error model known parameters (β=0.3\beta = 0.3, τ=0.5\tau = 0.5). 2. small_salinas_ensemble.csv small_salinas_obs.csv: Real-world Salinas SOC ensemble benchmark dataset.
code: # Side-note: R snippet used to generate observation fixtures from an error model set.seed(3) output_scale <- stats::sd(ensemble_mean)  relative_bias  <- 0.3 # 30% relative bias relative_error <- 0.5 # 50% relative error noise  simulated_observation <- ensemble_mean +   output_scale * (     relative_bias +       stats::rnorm(length(ensemble_mean), mean = 0, sd = relative_error)   )

title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: framework categorizes evaluation metrics two groups: BIAS / Mean Bias Error: 1N∑(m‾−oi)\frac{1}{N}\sum (\bar{m}_i - o_i). Quantifies systematic - -prediction. RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error): 1N∑(m‾−oi)2\sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum (\bar{m}_i - o_i)^2}. Overall magnitude error. MAE (Mean Absolute Error): 1N∑|m‾−oi|\frac{1}{N}\sum |\bar{m}_i - o_i|. L1 norm error distance. R2 (Squared Pearson Correlation): Coefficient determination indicating proportion variance explained. COVERAGE (Prediction Interval Coverage): Fraction observations falling within 90% ensemble prediction interval [q05,q95][q_{05}, q_{95}]. CRPS (Continuous Ranked Probability Score): Evaluates full predictive probability distribution observations using scoringRules::crps_sample() (analytical sample score fallback).
code: # Compute complete metric suite metrics_results <- compute_metrics(   aligned_df,   metrics = c("BIAS", "RMSE", "MAE", "R2", "COVERAGE", "CRPS") )  print(metrics_results) #>    Site     BIAS     RMSE      MAE        R2 COVERAGE     CRPS #> 1 SiteA -1.79172 3.612696 2.860899 0.7938417   0.4375 2.339759

what: Comparing Calculated Metrics against Theoretical Expectations
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: Since simulated observation fixture generated known statistical error parameters βv=0.3\beta_v = 0.3 τv=0.5\tau_v = 0.5, closed-form theoretical expected values can derived directly BIAS, RMSE, MAE, R2R^2: Output Scale (SvS_v): Sv=sd(m‾)S_v = \text{sd}(\bar{m}), computed dynamically ensemble mean predictions. Expected BIAS: E[m‾−o]=−βv⋅Sv\text{E}[\bar{m} - o] = -\beta_v \cdot S_v. Expected RMSE: E[(m‾−o)2]=Svβv2+τv2\sqrt{\text{E}[(\bar{m} - o)^2]} = S_v \sqrt{\beta_v^2 + \tau_v^2}. Expected MAE: residual e∼N(−βvSv,τv2Sv2)e \sim N(-\beta_v S_v, \tau_v^2 S_v^2), E[|e|]=σ2πexp⁡(−μ22σ2)+μ(1−2Φ(−μσ))\text{E}[|e|] = \sigma \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \exp\left(-\frac{\mu^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) + \mu \left( 1 - 2\Phi\left(-\frac{\mu}{\sigma}\right) \right). Expected R2R^2: Population coefficient determination m‾\bar{m} oo: 11+τv2\frac{1}{1 + \tau_v^2}. Comparison Closed-Form Theoretical Expectations vs. Empirical Calculated Metrics Key Takeaways & Interpretation: * BIAS: theoretical expected bias −βvSv=−0.3×6.31=−1.89-\beta_v S_v = -0.3 \times 6.31 = -1.89. empirical calculated bias fixture (-1.79) closely matches expectation. negative sign occurs +βvSv+\beta_v S_v added observations (o>m‾o > \bar{m}), m‾−o<0\bar{m} - o < 0. * RMSE & MAE: Theoretical expectations (3.68 RMSE 2.96 MAE) align closely empirical fixture metrics (3.61 2.86), confirming consistency across standard error norms. * R2R^2: population R2=11+τv2=11+0.52=0.80R^2 = \frac{1}{1 + \tau_v^2} = \frac{1}{1 + 0.5^2} = 0.80 matches empirical calculated value (0.79).
code: # Error model parameters used in simulation fixture generator beta_v  <- 0.3  # 30% relative bias tau_v   <- 0.5  # 50% relative error noise  # Output scale S_v = sd(ensemble_mean) computed from model summary S_v <- sd(model_summary$value)  # Closed-form theoretical expectations exp_bias <- -beta_v * S_v exp_rmse <- S_v * sqrt(beta_v^2 + tau_v^2)  mu    <- -beta_v * S_v sigma <- tau_v * S_v exp_mae  <- sigma * sqrt(2 / pi) * exp(-mu^2 / (2 * sigma^2)) + mu * (1 - 2 * pnorm(-mu / sigma))  exp_r2   <- 1 / (1 + tau_v^2)  # Format summary comparison table theoretical_comparison <- data.frame(   Metric = c("BIAS", "RMSE", "MAE", "R2"),   `Theoretical Expectation` = round(c(exp_bias, exp_rmse, exp_mae, exp_r2), 4),   `Empirical Calculated Metric` = round(as.numeric(metrics_results[1, c("BIAS", "RMSE", "MAE", "R2")]), 4),   check.names = FALSE )  knitr::kable(   theoretical_comparison,   caption = "Comparison of Closed-Form Theoretical Expectations vs. Empirical Calculated Metrics" )

what: 6. Substituting Custom Processed Data & Real-World EFI Example
title: PEcAn Benchmarking and Validation Framework Tutorial
text: evaluate custom model predictions observational datasets using PEcAn.benchmark framework: Model Predictions: Format model outputs standard EFI long format CSV (containing datetime time, site_id, parameter ensemble member ID, variable, prediction value). Observations: Format observations timestamps (time date), target values (value, obvs, obs_mean), uncertainty metrics (obvs_sd, obs_sd, obs_se). Array Extraction: Use efi_long_to_array(raw_model, var = "<variable>", site = "<site_id>") extract (Ntime×Nensemble)(N_{\text{time}} \times N_{\text{ensemble}}) ensemble matrix. Alignment & Metric Evaluation: Pass reshaped summaries align_by_time() compute point probabilistic evaluation metrics compute_metrics(). complete walkthrough demonstrating workflow real-world dataset EFI long format (small_salinas_ensemble.csv small_salinas_obs.csv):
code: salinas_model <- read.csv(file.path(extdata_dir, "small_salinas_ensemble.csv")) salinas_obs   <- read.csv(file.path(extdata_dir, "small_salinas_obs.csv"))  # Reshape EFI long format to ensemble matrix for site 'socs_sys1' sal_mat <- efi_long_to_array(salinas_model, var = "TotSoilCarb", site = "socs_sys1")  sal_model_summary <- data.frame(   time = attr(sal_mat, "time"),   value = rowMeans(sal_mat, na.rm = TRUE),   model_q05 = apply(sal_mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),   model_q95 = apply(sal_mat, 1, quantile, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),   site = "socs_sys1" )  sal_obs_filtered <- salinas_obs[salinas_obs$site_id == "socs_sys1" & salinas_obs$variable == "TotSoilCarb", ] sal_obs_summary <- data.frame(   time = as.POSIXct(sal_obs_filtered$date, tz = "UTC"),   value = sal_obs_filtered$obs_mean,   obvs_sd = sal_obs_filtered$obs_sd,   site = "socs_sys1" )  sal_aligned <- align_by_time(sal_model_summary, sal_obs_summary, tolerance_secs = 365 * 86400 / 2) sal_aligned_indices <- match(sal_aligned$time, sal_model_summary$time) attr(sal_aligned, "ensemble_matrix") <- sal_mat[sal_aligned_indices, , drop = FALSE]  sal_metrics <- compute_metrics(sal_aligned, metrics = c("BIAS", "RMSE", "MAE", "R2", "COVERAGE", "CRPS")) print(sal_metrics) #>        Site    BIAS     RMSE     MAE R2 COVERAGE     CRPS #> 1 socs_sys1 0.18915 0.193965 0.18915  1        1 0.210625

title: Squared Pearson Correlation (R2) — metric_R2
text: Computes R-squared using correlation-based formula: \(R^2 = \left(\frac{\sum(obs - \bar{obs})(mod - \bar{mod})} {\sqrt{\sum(obs - \bar{obs})^2} \cdot \sqrt{\sum(mod - \bar{mod})^2}}\right)^2\) Note: correlation-based R2, invariant bias slope. model perfectly correlated biased (e.g., model = obs + 100) still score 1. distinct variance explained Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE).
